lessons.title: Understanding V8 Heap, Stack, and Variable Scope
lessons.description: Learn how JavaScript allocates primitives and object references in memory stack vs heap.
lessons.theory:
### Memory Allocation in JavaScript

JavaScript manages memory automatically using a garbage collector based on mark-and-sweep algorithms.

- **Stack Memory**: Static data allocation for primitive types (numbers, booleans, strings). Fast, fixed-size.
- **Heap Memory**: Dynamic memory allocation for objects, arrays, and functions.

```javascript
let name = "CompetencyAI"; // Allocated on Call Stack
let user = { id: 101, role: "Engineer" }; // Object stored in Heap, reference stored in Stack
```
lessons.codeExamples: [{"label":"Stack vs Heap Example","code":"const a = 42;\nconst b = { key: \"val\" };"}]

questions.title: C Primitive Data Types
questions.prompt: Which of the following is the correct keyword for declaring a single character variable in C?
questions.explanation: In C programming, "char" is used to declare character variables.
questions.subject: C

questions.title: C++ Class Access Specifiers
questions.prompt: By default, what is the access specifier for members of a class in C++ if not specified?
questions.explanation: In C++, class members are private by default, whereas struct members are public by default.
questions.subject: C++

questions.title: Java Primitive Default Value
questions.prompt: What is the default value of an uninitialized boolean instance variable in Java?
questions.explanation: In Java, boolean instance fields default to false when initialized by the JVM.
questions.subject: Java

questions.title: HTML Boilerplate Document Type
questions.prompt: Which tag specifies the document type and HTML version for modern web browsers?
questions.explanation: <!DOCTYPE html> declares the document type as HTML5.
questions.subject: HTML

questions.title: Basic SQL Retrieval Query
questions.prompt: Which SQL clause is used to filter records based on a specified condition?
questions.explanation: The WHERE clause filters rows based on a boolean condition before grouping or sorting.
questions.codeSnippet: SELECT * FROM students ___ age >= 18;
questions.subject: SQL

questions.title: JavaScript Constant Declaration
questions.prompt: Which keyword is used to declare a block-scoped variable that cannot be reassigned in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: const creates a block-scoped constant variable reference in ES6+ JavaScript.
questions.subject: JavaScript

questions.title: HTTP Client Request Protocols
questions.prompt: Which HTTP method is primarily used to request data from a specified server resource without side effects?
questions.explanation: GET requests retrieve representation of data from the specified URI without modifying server state.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: C Post-increment Operator
questions.prompt: What is the output of the following C code snippet?
questions.explanation: The post-increment operator (x++) returns the current value (5) first and increments x to 6 afterward.
questions.subject: C

questions.title: C++ Default Constructor
questions.prompt: What is true regarding constructors in C++?
questions.explanation: A constructor has the exact same name as the class and does not specify any return type, not even void.
questions.subject: C++

questions.title: Web Application Tiers
questions.prompt: In a modern 3-tier web architecture, which layer executes directly inside the user's web browser?
questions.explanation: The presentation/client layer (Frontend) executes in the web browser using HTML, CSS, and JS.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: Java String Immutability
questions.prompt: What is the value of str after executing the following Java code?
questions.explanation: Strings in Java are immutable. concat() returns a new string, but str reference remains "Hello".
questions.subject: Java

questions.title: HTML Anchor Attribute
questions.prompt: Which attribute in an <a> tag specifies the destination URL of a hyperlink?
questions.explanation: The "href" attribute (hypertext reference) defines the target URL for hyperlinks.
questions.subject: HTML

questions.title: SQL Sorting Keyword
questions.prompt: Which clause is used in SQL to sort the query result set in descending order?
questions.explanation: DESC sorts records in descending order (ASC is default ascending).
questions.codeSnippet: SELECT * FROM products ORDER BY price ___;
questions.subject: SQL

questions.title: JavaScript typeof null Evaluation
questions.prompt: What does the typeof operator return for typeof null in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: In JavaScript, typeof null returns "object" due to a historical bug retained for backward compatibility.
questions.codeSnippet: console.log(typeof null);
questions.subject: JavaScript

questions.title: HTTP Status Code 201 Created
questions.prompt: Which HTTP response status code indicates that a request succeeded and led to the creation of a new resource?
questions.explanation: HTTP status 201 Created indicates successful request and resource creation on the server.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: C Loop Execution Bounds
questions.prompt: How many times will the loop print "IT" in the following C code?
questions.explanation: i starts at 0 (print), then 2 (print), then 4 (print). i becomes 6 and loop terminates. Printed 3 times.
questions.subject: C

questions.title: OOP Encapsulation Concept
questions.prompt: Wrapping data fields and methods together into a single unit in object-oriented programming is known as:
questions.explanation: Encapsulation binds together code and the data it manipulates into a single unit (class).
questions.subject: C++

questions.title: Java Switch Statement Data Types
questions.prompt: Which of the following data types is NOT supported in a standard Java switch statement (up to Java 7)?
questions.explanation: boolean expressions cannot be evaluated in a switch statement; only byte, short, char, int, String, and Enums are allowed.
questions.subject: Java

questions.title: JavaScript Implicit Return
questions.prompt: What does the following arrow function return?
questions.explanation: Concise arrow functions without curly braces implicitly return the evaluated expression (3 + 4 = 7).
questions.codeSnippet:
const add = (a, b) => a + b;
console.log(add(3, 4));
questions.subject: JavaScript

questions.title: JSON Valid Property Names
questions.prompt: In valid JSON syntax, how must property names/keys be formatted?
questions.explanation: JSON specification (RFC 8259) strictly requires property keys to be enclosed in double quotes.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: C Null Terminator Character
questions.prompt: What is the output of sizeof("Hello") in C on a standard platform?
questions.explanation: "Hello" consists of 5 letters plus 1 implicit null terminator ('\0'), giving a total size of 6 bytes.
questions.subject: C

questions.title: C++ Multiple Inheritance
questions.prompt: Which feature in C++ allows a derived class to inherit directly from more than one base class?
questions.explanation: C++ supports Multiple Inheritance where a single class can inherit attributes/methods from multiple base classes.
questions.subject: C++

questions.title: Java Super Keyword Usage
questions.prompt: Which Java keyword is used by a subclass constructor to invoke its immediate parent class constructor?
questions.explanation: super() is used inside a child class constructor to call the constructor of its parent class.
questions.subject: Java

questions.title: HTML Form Input Types
questions.prompt: Which HTML5 input type provides built-in email format validation natively in browser forms?
questions.explanation: <input type="email"> provides native pattern matching for email address formats.
questions.subject: HTML

questions.title: Filtering Grouped SQL Records
questions.prompt: Which SQL clause is used to filter records AFTER an aggregation or GROUP BY operation has occurred?
questions.explanation: HAVING is used to filter aggregated group records, whereas WHERE filters individual rows prior to grouping.
questions.codeSnippet: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY department_id ___ COUNT(*) > 5;
questions.subject: SQL

questions.title: JavaScript Array.map Output
questions.prompt: What is the output of the following JavaScript code?
questions.explanation: Array.map transforms every element according to the callback, producing [2, 4, 6].
questions.subject: JavaScript

questions.title: REST API Verbs Mapping
questions.prompt: In RESTful architecture, which HTTP verb corresponds directly to the "Update" action in CRUD?
questions.explanation: PUT or PATCH HTTP methods are used to update existing resources in REST APIs.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: C Pointer Dereferencing
questions.prompt: What will be printed by the following C code?
questions.explanation: *ptr dereferences pointer ptr and fetches the value stored at memory address &num (10).
questions.subject: C

questions.title: C++ Virtual Function Purpose
questions.prompt: What keyword enables dynamic/runtime polymorphism (late binding) for member functions in C++?
questions.explanation: The "virtual" keyword instructs the compiler to perform dynamic dispatch using a VTable at runtime.
questions.subject: C++

questions.title: HTTP Status Code 500 Error Class
questions.prompt: What does an HTTP status code in the 5xx range (such as 500 Internal Server Error) signify?
questions.explanation: 5xx status codes indicate server-side processing errors when handling client requests.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: Java Multiple Inheritance via Interfaces
questions.prompt: How does Java achieve multiple inheritance of type behavior?
questions.explanation: Java does not support multiple class inheritance, but allows a class to implement multiple interfaces.
questions.subject: Java

questions.title: Semantic HTML Elements
questions.prompt: Which tag is a semantic HTML5 container specifically intended for independent, self-contained content like articles or blog posts?
questions.explanation: <article> represents a self-contained composition intended to be independently distributable.
questions.subject: HTML

questions.title: SQL LEFT JOIN Behavior
questions.prompt: What does a LEFT JOIN return between Table A (Left) and Table B (Right)?
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN returns all records from Table A, and matched records from Table B (filling NULL for non-matches).
questions.codeSnippet: SELECT A.name, B.order_date FROM Customers A LEFT JOIN Orders B ON A.id = B.customer_id;
questions.subject: SQL

questions.title: JavaScript Variable Hoisting
questions.prompt: What is printed to the console when executing the following code?
questions.explanation: var declarations are hoisted to top of scope initialized with undefined before execution.
questions.codeSnippet:
console.log(a);
var a = 10;
questions.subject: JavaScript

questions.title: Browser LocalStorage Properties
questions.prompt: Which client-side storage mechanism persists data across browser window tabs and survives browser restarts?
questions.explanation: localStorage data has no expiration date and persists until explicitly cleared via JS or browser storage clear.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: C Structure vs Union Memory
questions.prompt: What is the primary difference between a struct and a union in C?
questions.explanation: In a struct, each member gets its own unique memory location; in a union, all members share the same memory space.
questions.subject: C

questions.title: C++ Function Overloading Rules
questions.prompt: Which of the following conditions is required for valid function overloading in C++?
questions.explanation: Overloaded functions must differ in their parameter list (number, type, or order of parameters). Different return types alone are invalid.
questions.subject: C++

questions.title: Java finally Block Execution
questions.prompt: What is guaranteed about the finally block in Java exception handling?
questions.explanation: The finally block executes whether an exception is thrown or caught (unless System.exit() occurs). Output: Catch Finally
questions.subject: Java

questions.title: JavaScript Event Delegation
questions.prompt: What is Event Delegation in DOM manipulation?
questions.explanation: Event Delegation attaches a single event listener to a parent element to handle events on its child elements via event bubbling.
questions.subject: JavaScript

questions.title: Express.js next() Function Purpose
questions.prompt: In Express.js middleware functions, what is the role of the next() parameter?
questions.explanation: Calling next() passes control to the next middleware function in the stack.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: C Memory Allocation malloc vs calloc
questions.prompt: What is the key difference between malloc() and calloc() in C memory management?
questions.explanation: calloc() allocates memory and initializes all bytes to zero, whereas malloc() leaves memory uninitialized with garbage values.
questions.subject: C

questions.title: C++ std::map Internal Data Structure
questions.prompt: What underlying data structure is typically used to implement std::map in the C++ Standard Template Library (STL)?
questions.explanation: std::map is typically implemented as a self-balancing Red-Black Binary Search Tree ensuring O(log N) operations.
questions.subject: C++

questions.title: Java ArrayList vs LinkedList Access Complexity
questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of element random access by index (get(i)) in ArrayList vs LinkedList in Java?
questions.explanation: ArrayList provides O(1) constant time index access via array backing; LinkedList requires O(N) traversal.
questions.subject: Java

questions.title: HTML ARIA Accessibility Attributes
questions.prompt: What does WAI-ARIA stand for in web accessibility and HTML design?
questions.explanation: WAI-ARIA stands for Web Accessibility Initiative - Accessible Rich Internet Applications.
questions.subject: HTML

questions.title: SQL Correlated Subquery
questions.prompt: What defines a Correlated Subquery in SQL?
questions.explanation: A correlated subquery evaluates once for each row processed by the outer query because it references columns from the outer query table.
questions.codeSnippet: SELECT e1.name FROM employees e1 WHERE e1.salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees e2 WHERE e2.dept_id = e1.dept_id);
questions.subject: SQL

questions.title: JavaScript Async Promise Execution Order
questions.prompt: What will be logged to the console by the following script?
questions.explanation: Synchronous code logs "A" then "C". Promise callback is queued in Microtask Queue and executes after synchronous stack, logging "B". Output: A C B
questions.subject: JavaScript

questions.title: React Props Immutability
questions.prompt: In React component architecture, how do props differ fundamentally from state?
questions.explanation: Props are read-only immutable inputs passed from parent components; state is internal mutable data managed within the component.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: C Pre-increment vs Post-increment in Expressions
questions.prompt: What is the output of the following C program?
questions.explanation: ++a increments a from 5 to 6. Expressions evaluation with sequence point yields 6 + 6 = 12 (and a becomes 7 after). Output: 12.
questions.subject: C

questions.title: C++ Reference Instantiation Rule
questions.prompt: Which statement is TRUE regarding C++ references (&)?
questions.explanation: A C++ reference must be bound to an object upon declaration and cannot be reassigned to refer to another object or set to NULL.
questions.subject: C++

questions.title: React useEffect Dependency Array
questions.prompt: When does a React useEffect hook run if an empty dependency array ([]) is passed as the second argument?
questions.explanation: An empty dependency array ([]) causes useEffect to run only once after the initial component mount.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: Java HashMap Collision Handling
questions.prompt: In Java 8+, what data structure does HashMap switch to when bucket chain size exceeds 8 (TREEIFY_THRESHOLD)?
questions.explanation: In Java 8, when a bucket linked list exceeds 8 items, HashMap converts the bucket into a Red-Black Tree to improve lookup from O(N) to O(log N).
questions.subject: Java

questions.title: HTML Form enctype for File Uploads
questions.prompt: Which enctype value must be set on an HTML <form> when submitting binary file inputs via POST?
questions.explanation: multipart/form-data is required for uploading binary files or text mixed with files via HTML form POST.
questions.subject: HTML

questions.title: SQL Foreign Key Referential Integrity
questions.prompt: What constraint error is raised when deleting a row in a parent table that is referenced by rows in a child table with default FOREIGN KEY constraint?
questions.explanation: Referential integrity constraints prevent deleting parent rows if active child references exist without CASCADE rule.
questions.subject: SQL

questions.title: JavaScript Fetch HTTP Error Status Handling
questions.prompt: Does window.fetch() reject its returned Promise on an HTTP 404 Not Found response?
questions.explanation: fetch() only rejects a Promise on network failure or request blocking. HTTP 404/500 resolve successfully with res.ok = false.
questions.subject: JavaScript

questions.title: JSON Web Token (JWT) Structure
questions.prompt: A JSON Web Token (JWT) consists of three dot-separated parts in which sequence?
questions.explanation: JWT format is Header.Payload.Signature encoded in Base64URL.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: C Pointer Addition Arithmetic
questions.prompt: Assuming int is 4 bytes and ptr points to memory address 1000, what is the value of (ptr + 2)?
questions.explanation: Pointer arithmetic increments address by (offset * sizeof(type)). 1000 + (2 * 4 bytes) = 1008.
questions.subject: C

questions.title: C++ Catch-All Handler Syntax
questions.prompt: Which catch block syntax catches any uncaught exception type in C++?
questions.explanation: catch(...) is the universal catch-all handler in C++ exception handling.
questions.subject: C++

questions.title: Java Runnable vs Thread Execution
questions.prompt: Which method must be called to start execution of a new background thread in Java?
questions.explanation: Calling start() allocates a new call stack and invokes run() asynchronously. Calling run() directly runs on current thread.
questions.codeSnippet:
Thread t = new Thread(runnableTask);
// How to start thread t?
questions.subject: Java

questions.title: JavaScript Object Spread Merge
questions.prompt: What is the value of obj3 after executing the following ES6 code?
questions.explanation: The spread operator shallow merges properties from left to right; obj2.b (99) overwrites obj1.b (2).
questions.subject: JavaScript

questions.title: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)
questions.prompt: Which HTTP response header enables a backend server to allow frontend web applications from another domain to access its API resources?
questions.explanation: Access-Control-Allow-Origin controls cross-origin access permissions in browsers.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: C Bitwise XOR Operation
questions.prompt: What is the output of the expression (5 ^ 3) in C?
questions.explanation: 5 is 0101 in binary, 3 is 0011 in binary. Bitwise XOR (0101 ^ 0011) = 0110 in binary, which equals 6.
questions.subject: C

questions.title: C++ Shallow vs Deep Copy Problem
questions.prompt: Why is a custom Copy Constructor necessary for C++ classes containing dynamically allocated pointer members?
questions.explanation: Default copy constructors perform shallow copy (copying pointer addresses), leading to double-free errors when destructors run.
questions.subject: C++

questions.title: Java Garbage Collection Eligibility
questions.prompt: When does an object on the Java Heap Memory become eligible for Garbage Collection (GC)?
questions.explanation: An object becomes eligible for GC when it is no longer reachable from any active thread GC root reference.
questions.subject: Java

questions.title: HTML5 Canvas vs SVG Rendering
questions.prompt: What is a key difference between HTML5 <canvas> and Inline SVG graphic rendering?
questions.explanation: <canvas> is pixel-based raster rendering (immediate mode); SVG is XML vector-based (retained mode with DOM nodes for elements).
questions.subject: HTML

questions.title: Third Normal Form (3NF) Requirement
questions.prompt: What condition must a database table satisfy to comply with Third Normal Form (3NF)?
questions.explanation: 3NF requires that the table is in 2NF and contains no transitive functional dependencies (non-prime attributes depending on non-prime attributes).
questions.subject: SQL

questions.title: JavaScript Event Loop Queue Priority
questions.prompt: In Node.js/V8 Event Loop processing, what is executed first after the current synchronous stack finishes: Microtask Queue or Macrotask (Task) Queue?
questions.explanation: Microtask Queue (Promises, process.nextTick) is processed completely before picking the next Macrotask (setTimeout). Output: Promise, Timeout.
questions.codeSnippet:
setTimeout(() => console.log("Timeout"), 0);
Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log("Promise"));
questions.subject: JavaScript

questions.title: Preventing SQL Injection Attacks
questions.prompt: What is the most effective engineering defense against SQL Injection vulnerabilities in backend web applications?
questions.explanation: Using Prepared Statements with Parameterized Queries separates SQL code from user data, preventing query structure manipulation.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: C Recursion Base Case Absence
questions.prompt: What runtime error occurs if a recursive C function lacks a proper terminating base condition?
questions.explanation: Infinite recursion exhausts call stack frame memory leading to Stack Overflow runtime crash.
questions.subject: C

questions.title: C++ std::unique_ptr Ownership Transfer
questions.prompt: How is ownership of a managed object transferred from one std::unique_ptr to another in C++11?
questions.explanation: std::unique_ptr cannot be copied (copy constructor deleted); ownership must be transferred using std::move().
questions.codeSnippet:
std::unique_ptr<int> p1 = std::make_unique<int>(42);
// How to transfer ownership to p2?
questions.subject: C++

questions.title: Cryptographic Password Salting Purpose
questions.prompt: Why is a cryptographic Salt added to user passwords before hashing them (e.g. using bcrypt or PBKDF2)?
questions.explanation: Salting prevents Rainbow Table lookups and ensures identical passwords produce distinct hash values.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: Java String Pool Operator Comparison
questions.prompt: What will be printed by the following Java code snippet?
questions.explanation: s1 and s2 refer to the exact same String Pool literal (s1 == s2 is true). s3 creates a new object in Heap (s1 == s3 is false). Output: true false
questions.subject: Java

questions.title: SQL Aggregate Grouping Condition
questions.prompt: Which query retrieves departments with an average salary exceeding 50000 alongside total employee count?
questions.explanation: GROUP BY dept_id HAVING AVG(salary) > 50000 filters aggregated groups.
questions.codeSnippet: SELECT dept_id, COUNT(*), AVG(salary) FROM employees ___ ___ > 50000;
questions.subject: SQL

questions.title: JavaScript Loop Closure with var vs let
questions.prompt: What is printed to the console after 100ms when executing the following code?
questions.explanation: var is function-scoped. By the time setTimeout callbacks execute, the single shared loop variable i has incremented to 3. Output: 3 3 3.
questions.subject: JavaScript

questions.title: Node.js Event-Driven Architecture
questions.prompt: How does Node.js handle high-concurrency I/O operations despite running main application JavaScript on a single thread?
questions.explanation: Node.js delegates asynchronous I/O operations to the underlying OS or libuv thread pool, receiving completion notifications on the Event Loop.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: C Memory Leak Identification
questions.prompt: Which utility tool is widely used on Linux systems to detect memory leaks and invalid heap accesses in compiled C programs?
questions.explanation: Valgrind (specifically the Memcheck tool) analyzes binary memory allocations to flag memory leaks and uninitialized memory access.
questions.subject: C

questions.title: C++ Generic Function Template Syntax
questions.prompt: Which line correctly declares a C++ function template returning the maximum of two values of generic type T?
questions.explanation: template <typename T> T getMax(T a, T b) defines a generic template function.
questions.subject: C++

questions.title: Java Checked vs Unchecked Exceptions
questions.prompt: Which class must a custom Exception extend in Java to be categorized as an Unchecked (Runtime) Exception?
questions.explanation: Custom unchecked exceptions must extend java.lang.RuntimeException (or its subclasses).
questions.subject: Java

questions.title: JavaScript Prototype Inheritance Lookup
questions.prompt: What will be printed when executing the following code?
questions.explanation: u.role does not exist directly on instance u (delete has no effect on prototype). Lookup delegates up prototype chain to User.prototype.role ("Learner").
questions.subject: JavaScript

questions.title: Secrets Management in Production
questions.prompt: Why should production database passwords and secret JWT keys NEVER be hardcoded into git version control source files?
questions.explanation: Committing secrets into source control exposes credentials to unauthorized repository access and history leaks. They must be injected via environment variables.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: Git Merge Conflict Resolution Flow
questions.prompt: When Git flags a merge conflict between two branches, what sequence of actions resolves it properly?
questions.explanation: Conflict markers must be manually resolved in the file, then git add <file> stages the resolved file, followed by git commit.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: C Pointer to Pointer Evaluation
questions.prompt: What is the output of the following C program?
questions.explanation: **pp double dereferences to variable a and updates its value to 50. Output: 50.
questions.subject: C

questions.title: C++ Base Class Virtual Destructor Importance
questions.prompt: Why must a polymorphic base class in C++ declare a virtual destructor?
questions.explanation: If a base class destructor is not virtual, executing "delete ptr" on a Base pointer to a Derived object only calls the Base destructor, causing undefined behavior and resource leaks.
questions.codeSnippet:
Base *ptr = new Derived();
delete ptr;
questions.subject: C++

questions.title: Java Thread Deadlock Condition
questions.prompt: Which set of 4 Coffman conditions must hold simultaneously for a Thread Deadlock to occur in Java concurrent programming?
questions.explanation: Deadlock requires: Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, and Circular Wait.
questions.subject: Java

questions.title: JavaScript Function Currying Output
questions.prompt: What is returned by evaluating multiply(2)(3)(4) given the following curried function definition?
questions.explanation: Curried functions evaluate nested unary functions: 2 * 3 * 4 = 24.
questions.codeSnippet:
const multiply = a => b => c => a * b * c;
console.log(multiply(2)(3)(4));
questions.subject: JavaScript

questions.title: Monolithic vs Microservice Tradeoff
questions.prompt: What is a major architectural challenge introduced when transitioning from a Monolith to Microservices?
questions.explanation: Microservices introduce distributed system complexity, requiring network fault tolerance, eventual consistency, and distributed tracing.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: C fflush(stdout) Purpose
questions.prompt: What is the purpose of calling fflush(stdout) in C network or console programming?
questions.explanation: fflush(stdout) forces the output stream buffer to write its buffered contents immediately to the underlying device or terminal.
questions.subject: C

questions.title: C++ RAII Idiom
questions.prompt: What does the RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) idiom guarantee in C++ software engineering?
questions.explanation: RAII ties resource lifecycle (files, memory, locks) to object lifetime, ensuring automatic cleanup when objects go out of scope.
questions.subject: C++

questions.title: Java Generics Bounded Wildcard (PECS)
questions.prompt: In Java Generics design principles, what does the mnemonic PECS stand for?
questions.explanation: PECS stands for Producer Extends, Consumer Super (use ? extends T for data sources, ? super T for data sinks).
questions.subject: Java

questions.title: Debounce vs Throttle Functions
questions.prompt: In high-frequency event handling (like window resize or search inputs), how does Debouncing differ from Throttling?
questions.explanation: Debouncing delays execution until events pause for N ms; Throttling limits execution to at most once per fixed time interval N ms.
questions.subject: JavaScript

questions.title: Token Bucket Algorithm for Rate Limiting
questions.prompt: Which algorithmic pattern is commonly used in Redis API Rate Limiting middleware to permit bursts while enforcing average request throughput?
questions.explanation: The Token Bucket algorithm adds tokens to a bucket at a fixed rate, allowing bursts up to bucket capacity.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: C Structure Memory Alignment Padding
questions.prompt: On a 64-bit architecture with 4-byte int and 8-byte pointer alignment, what is sizeof(struct Data)?
questions.explanation: char c (1 byte) + 3 padding bytes, int i (4 bytes) = 8 bytes. double d (8 bytes). Total aligned size = 16 bytes.
questions.subject: C

questions.title: C++11 Rvalue References (&&)
questions.prompt: What primary problem do Move Semantics and Rvalue References (&&) solve in modern C++11?
questions.explanation: Move semantics eliminate expensive deep copies when transferring resources from temporary rvalue objects to lvalue targets.
questions.subject: C++

questions.title: Java ConcurrentHashMap Lock Granularity
questions.prompt: How does ConcurrentHashMap achieve high concurrency without locking the entire table during write operations in Java 8+?
questions.explanation: Java 8 ConcurrentHashMap uses fine-grained CAS (Compare-And-Swap) operations and synchronized lock nodes on individual bucket heads rather than locking table segments.
questions.subject: Java

questions.title: SQL Database B-Tree Index Lookup Complexity
questions.prompt: Why are B-Tree indexes preferred over Hash indexes for relational database columns evaluated with range queries (e.g. BETWEEN or >)?
questions.explanation: B-Trees store keys in sorted order, enabling fast logarithmic sequential range scans; Hash indexes only support O(1) exact equality matches.
questions.subject: SQL

questions.title: JavaScript WeakMap Key Garbage Collection
questions.prompt: How does a WeakMap differ from a standard Map regarding memory leak management in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: WeakMap keys must be objects and are held weakly, allowing keys to be garbage collected if no other references exist, preventing memory leaks.
questions.subject: JavaScript

questions.title: Sticky Sessions vs Stateless Load Balancing
questions.prompt: In a scaled production deployment with multiple API server instances, why is Stateless JWT Session Architecture preferred over Server-Stored Sticky Sessions?
questions.explanation: Stateless JWTs allow any server instance to verify and process requests independently, enabling seamless horizontal scaling without session-affinity binding.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Mitigation
questions.prompt: Which security header instructs modern web browsers to block inline script execution and enforce strict trusted script source domains?
questions.explanation: Content-Security-Policy (CSP) headers prevent XSS by restricting allowed script sources and disallowing unsafe inline scripts.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: SQL Transaction Isolation Levels
questions.prompt: Which SQL Transaction Isolation Level completely prevents Dirty Reads, Non-Repeatable Reads, and Phantom Reads?
questions.explanation: SERIALIZABLE is the highest isolation level, executing transactions sequentially to eliminate all read anomalies.
questions.subject: Full Stack

questions.title: Next.js Rendering Strategies
questions.prompt: Which rendering strategy in Next.js generates static HTML pages at build time and re-generates individual pages in the background on incoming requests without rebuilding the full app?
questions.explanation: Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR) enables updating static pages incrementally after build time.
questions.subject: Full Stack
questions.topic: SSR vs CSR vs SSG Architecture

questions.title: Blue-Green Deployment Strategy
questions.prompt: How does Blue-Green Deployment ensure zero-downtime updates during production web app releases?
questions.explanation: Blue-Green maintains two identical environments; new version is deployed to idle Green env and load balancer router switches traffic seamlessly once health checks pass.
questions.subject: Full Stack
